record.what_it_does: GitHub is a hosted Git platform for source code, issues, pull requests, Actions/CI, and project management, exposed via REST and GraphQL APIs.
record.auth_notes: GitHub Apps (recommended over legacy OAuth Apps) use OAuth 2.0 to act on behalf of a user with fine-grained permissions and short-lived tokens; a JWT signed with the app's private key is used to generate GitHub App installation access tokens. Personal access tokens (fine-grained or classic) are static Bearer tokens sent as `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN`. Basic auth (client_id/client_secret) is used only for specific app-management endpoints like token-checking. Username/password auth is not supported.
record.access_notes: Any developer can immediately create a personal access token or register an OAuth App/GitHub App for free with no paid plan required; some endpoints/features (e.g. certain Copilot or Enterprise endpoints) require a paid plan, but core API access is free and self-serve.
